output.summary: KEP-1301 proposed using RuntimeClass (plus a node.kubernetes.io/windows-build label, a RuntimeHandler in the CRI pull API, and per-RuntimeClass containerd config) to schedule Windows pods to compatible nodes and to control Hyper-V isolation. Current status is implementable at stage alpha.
output.rationale: The problem is that Kubernetes scheduling relies only on the Pod spec, so a Pod can land on an incompatible Windows or multi-arch node and fail to pull, and user intent is ambiguous when a node can run several OS/version/arch permutations. The proposal routes these controls through RuntimeClass rather than new Pod API fields. Discussion shows the user-facing node label shipped in 1.17, while the CRI/RuntimeClass work slipped and the enhancement was tracked with fewer implementation PRs after 2020-09.

alternatives.option: Annotations instead of RuntimeClass for the CRI and containerd runtime selection
alternatives.why_not: Described as a fallback plan only; the proposal prefers RuntimeClass because Linux Kata on containerd is moving away from annotations, and in 2020 the team implemented the fallback with annotations in 1.19 for alpha.

alternatives.option: Adding new fields to the Pod API and changing Kubernetes scheduling behavior
alternatives.why_not: The Summary states the proposal controls these features through RuntimeClass 'rather than adding new fields to the Pod API and changing Kubernetes scheduling behavior'.

alternatives.option: Node selectors or taints per Pod for OS and version
alternatives.why_not: The Motivation calls these workable but cumbersome; the goal is 'a simpler experience (fewer lines of YAML) than adding os and version nodeSelector and tolerations to each Pod'.

evidence.quote: This document proposes controlling those features through RuntimeClass as well, rather than adding new fields to the Pod API and changing Kubernetes scheduling behavior.
